title: Early repertoire: pop songs, Clarence Rand and Ethel Waters records
summary: At first he sang jazz and popular songs learned from the radio and Victrola, including Clarence Rand's theme and an Ethel Waters record.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Growing up with radio, records and family listening

blocks.x: By then, what kind of songs were you singing? Were you singing...is that when you were singing jazz, or were you singing the blues by then?
I was singing jazz. I was singing all the songs that they had out popular.

I used to remember they had a fellow called Clarence Rand. That was before Bing Crosby's time, and he used to had a theme song, and I used to like the way he sing his theme song so I learned it. But now it slips my mind what the name of it was. And I used to listen to the radio and listen to all that music on the radio, and we had a wind-up Victrola at my house, and we had some records of all the old-time singers and stuff, and one record that I liked was Ethel Waters. She was singing on a record, "Shoo Shoo Boogie Boo, I'm sick and tired of you. Find your place behind the moon..." So I liked that, so I used to

always get together with the boys and learn the words, and we'd sing it. We have a good time. We had a big park we used to go play in and right by the boulevard, and we used to sit there and count the cars go by, and we'd stamp 'em and pick out the Ford, the Chevrolet. What cars we know we could pick 'em off, and we sit there and have fun stampin' them. See who could get the most stamps--how many cars went by.
